history: Autódromo Internacional de Tarumã, located near Viamão, Rio Grande do Sul, has been a cornerstone of Brazilian motorsport since its inauguration in 1970. The circuit has hosted numerous national championships, including Stock Car Brasil and Formula Truck. While the longer Internacional layout is more widely known, the Short Circuit configuration offers a unique challenge and has been used for regional events and driver development programs. Its shorter length makes it ideal for categories like Formula Vee and certain touring car classes, providing close racing and a good learning environment for up-and-coming drivers. The circuit has seen significant upgrades over the years to improve safety and facilities, maintaining its relevance in the modern racing landscape.
atmosphere: The air at Tarumã during a race on the Short Circuit is electric. The roar of engines echoes off the surrounding hills, creating an intense soundscape. The compact nature of the layout means spectators are never far from the action, providing a visceral experience as cars jostle for position through the tight corners. The vibrant Brazilian flags wave proudly, and the smell of grilled meats fills the air, adding to the festive atmosphere. The passion of the local fans is palpable, creating a true celebration of motorsport.
trackCharacter: The Short Circuit at Tarumã is a tight and technical layout that emphasizes car control and precision. With only six turns spread across 2.2 kilometers, the circuit demands constant attention from the drivers. Momentum is key, as maintaining speed through the flowing sections is crucial for a fast lap time. The layout rewards drivers who are aggressive yet smooth, able to exploit every inch of the track without sacrificing stability. It's a layout that favors nimble cars and confident drivers.

famousCorners.name: Curva 1
famousCorners.description: The opening right-hander is deceptively challenging, requiring a delicate balance of braking and throttle control.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining the right entry speed without compromising the exit is critical for carrying momentum onto the following straight.

famousCorners.name: Curva 2
famousCorners.description: A quick left-hander that immediately follows Curva 1, demanding a rapid transition and precise placement.
famousCorners.challenge: Requires a very quick flick of the steering wheel to get the car settled before the next corner

famousCorners.name: Curva 3
famousCorners.description: A tight right-hand hairpin which is a key overtaking spot.
famousCorners.challenge: A very slow corner, it's easy to outbrake yourself and run wide, losing time and position.

famousCorners.name: Curva 5
famousCorners.description: A fast, sweeping right-hander leading onto the main straight
famousCorners.challenge: Requires commitment and a good setup to carry maximum speed through this corner.

overtakingSpots: Late apex on the exit of Curva 5

The Short Circuit is used for regional championships and driver development programs.
Tarumã is located close to the city of Viamão.
The track has undergone several safety upgrades throughout its history.
Stock Car Brasil races are a highlight of the racing calendar at Tarumã.
The Short Circuit provides a different challenge compared to the longer Internacional layout.
weatherNotes: The weather in Rio Grande do Sul can be unpredictable, with sudden rain showers being a common occurrence. This can significantly impact grip levels on the Short Circuit, making tire management crucial. Humidity can also play a role, affecting engine performance and driver fatigue. Temperature fluctuations can also affect the track surface and therefore grip available.
drivingAdvice: On the Short Circuit, focus on maximizing corner exit speed, especially out of Curva 3, as it leads onto a crucial straight. Be aggressive on the brakes into Curva 1 and Curva 3, but avoid locking up as this can compromise your exit. The track rewards smooth inputs and a patient approach. Be mindful of tire wear, as the abrasive surface can take its toll over a race distance. Experiment with different lines through the flowing sections to find the optimal balance between speed and stability.
famousRaces: Regional Formula Vee championships often feature close battles on the Short Circuit, providing a platform for young drivers to hone their skills.
Local touring car series regularly utilize the Short Circuit, offering exciting sprint races with plenty of overtaking opportunities.
Historic racing events sometimes incorporate the Short Circuit to showcase classic cars in a more manageable and accessible format.
localCulture: The area surrounding Tarumã is rich in gaucho culture, characterized by its strong agricultural traditions and passion for horses. The local cuisine features hearty dishes like churrasco (barbecue) and chimarrão (a traditional mate drink). Paddock life is friendly and welcoming, with a strong sense of community among the teams and drivers. The locals are passionate about motorsport and are always eager to share their enthusiasm with visitors.
